The selected vendors will provide services as outlined in this RFP to assist clients with their daily needs and to help them move out of the shelter system as quickly as possible.

The mission of DHS is to prevent homelessness when possible and to provide short-term emergency shelter for individuals and families who have no other housing options available. DHS primarily meets this goal by providing services to clients in long-term contracted purpose-built shelters throughout the City. When there are not enough available shelter beds and units in traditional shelters, DHS temporarily uses commercial hotels to house clients while they transition to permanent housing.

item.title: Advance & Earn programs
item.description:
Youth and Community Development | Procurement | Award | $5.7M | Vendor: Goddard Riverside Community Center | Flagged: Contract value ≥ $1M

DYCD is seeking a qualified vendors to provide Advance & Earn programs in New York City. The populations served by the programs that are the subject of this NAE are adults that are seeking qualified organizations to provide new education and workforce development programs for opportunity youth (young adults ages 16-24 who are not in school and not working). Advance & Earn will help further their career through comprehensive High School Equivalency (HSE) test preparation, employer-recognized trainings, credentials and certifications, and paid internships. The program will combine services currently offered through DYCDs Young Adult Literacy Program (YALP) and Intern & Earn (formerly Young Adult Internship Program [YAIP]). The new programs will offer a continuum of education and employment services from literacy instruction through advanced training and job placement or college enrollment supported by comprehensive support services tailored to individual needs.

item.title: FY 27 Compass Center Based NAQ
item.description:
Youth and Community Development | Procurement | Intent to Award | Due: 2026-08-06 | Flagged: Contract value ≥ $1M

In accordance with section 3-04(b)(2)(i)(D) of the Procurement Policy Board Rules, the Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD) intends to negotiate the Comprehensive After-School System (COMPASS) Center Based Programs. The COMPASS Center Based Programs provides after-school services tailored to 6-8 Middle school youth. COMPASS offers high quality programs that have a strong balance of academics, recreation, enrichment, and cultural activities to support and strengthen the overall development of youth. COMPASS aims to help young people build skills to support their academic achievement, raise their confidence and cultivate their leadership skills through service learning and other civic engagement opportunities.

The term of this contract extension shall be for period of September 1, 2026, to August 31, 2027, with a one-year option to renew.

item.title: Defensive Driving Services
item.description:
Citywide Administrative Services | Procurement | Award | $375K | Vendor: National Traffic Safety Institute Corporation | Flagged: Sole-source / non-competitive

DCAS is requesting to extend the contract for 18 months from February 28, 2026, to August 27, 2027 to continue defensive driving services with National Traffic Safety Institute Corporation (NTSI) through the Negotiated Acquisition Extension procurement method pursuant to §3-04(b)(2)(iii) of the Procurement Policy Board Rules.

The cost of this NAE will be $375,000.00. This extension is needed while DCAS works on an RFP for a new contract. DCAS is currently in the evaluation process to award a vendor.

The term of the original contract was March 1, 2017, through February 28, 2020.

DCAS renewed the contract CT1856 20205401621 for a period of 3 years term from February 29, 2020 through February 27, 2023.

DCAS has exercised the 1-year ACCO extension, from February 28, 2023 through February 27, 2024. DCAS has exercised the first NAE(CT120248806088) from February 28, 2024 through February 27, 2025.

DCAS has exercised the second NAE (CTI 20258807034) from February 28, 2025 through February 27, 2026 and will be utilizing a third NAE.

Through this RFQ series, NYCHA is administering a pilot procurement that introduces a streamlined bid submission and evaluation process, differing from NYCHA's conventional solicitation procedures. The pilot is intended to simplify the solicitation process for responding bidders while supporting NYCHA's ongoing efforts to strengthen competition, improve efficiency, and enhance transparency within the Authority's procurement process.

At the time of RFQ closing, responding bidders will only be required to submit the minimum documentation identified in the solicitation. Following bid opening, NYCHA will evaluate bid pricing and identify the apparent low bidder(s). COMPASS and SONYC is one of DYCD's largest programs, with over 820 programs collectively throughout the five boroughs. Families rely on these programs to provide elementary and middle school students, during after school hours, summer and on holidays, programing which includes educational support, recreation, enrichment, and cultural activities to support and strengthen the overall development of our youth. Programs are offered at no cost to youth and are purposefully located in public and private schools, community centers, religious institutions, public housing and parks recreational facilities throughout the City to help families find a place that best fits their youth's needs.

item.title: SMD_A&CM_RFQ #518124 - Elevator Rehabilitation at Marcy Houses
item.description:
Housing Authority | Procurement | Solicitation | Due: 2026-08-27 | Flagged: Key-agency activity

The Work under this Contract (RFQ No. 518124  Elevator Package) consists of the rehabilitation, modernization, maintenance, and service of seventy (70) elevators across twenty-seven (27) residential buildings at Marcy Houses. The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and incidental services necessary to complete the Work in accordance with the Contract Documents.

The scope includes, but is not limited to, the removal and replacement of existing elevator systems and the furnishing and installation of new elevator equipment, including machines, controls, hoistway components, car enclosures, doors, communication systems, safety devices, and associated electrical components. The Work also includes testing, inspection, commissioning, training, and coordination with NYCHA and other trades, including a separate electrical contract.

item.description:
City Planning | Special Materials | Notice | Flagged: Special Materials (non-routine)

ADJUSTMENT IN HUDSON YARDS DISTRICT IMPROVEMENT BONUS CONTRIBUTION AMOUNT

 

As provided in Section 93-31 of the Zoning Resolution of the City of New York, the required contribution amount per square foot of bonused floor area available through the District Improvement Fund Bonus in the Special Hudson Yards District has been increased from $169.68 per square foot to $175.62 per square foot as of August 1, 2026. 

In accordance with Section 93-31, this increase is based on the change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI), as published by the U.S. Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics.  The CPI change for the period between July 1, 2025 and July 1, 2026 was an increase of 3.5 percent.
